critique.good: The grouped headers are clear, corresponding control and variant columns have similar proportions, and all values and intervals remain on one line. The p-value header also stays intact.
critique.problems: Most metric labels wrap, making six of the seven data rows tall. The repeated breaks weaken the labels as scanning anchors and leave substantial empty space beside the shorter numeric entries.
critique.cause: The 161px metric column leaves only 140px for text, while the 134px and 131px confidence-interval columns reserve enough space for every interval.

critique.good: The wider metric column keeps most labels on one line, and the paired control and variant columns are balanced. Percentage intervals remain easy to compare.
critique.problems: The time means split between minutes and seconds, and the currency and time intervals wrap. The p-value header also breaks across two lines. These breaks interrupt comparison within rows.
critique.cause: The 71px and 70px mean columns are too narrow for the complete time values; the 105px interval columns cannot hold the longest intervals; and the 75px p-value column is just too narrow for its header.

critique.good: Most metric labels fit on one line, and the matching widths reinforce the parallel control and variant groups.
critique.problems: Several percentage intervals now wrap as well as the currency and time intervals, creating tall rows and making endpoints harder to compare. The time means and p-value header also split. The extra label width does not keep the longest label on one line.
critique.cause: The 250px metric column takes space from the two 90px interval columns. The 71px and 70px mean columns and 75px p-value column retain the wrapping seen in r0B.

critique.good: The control and variant groups have balanced proportions, and their means, percentage intervals, lift values and p-values scan cleanly across each row. Metric labels wrap at sensible word boundaries.
critique.problems: The checkout completion label wraps, while both currency and time intervals break across lines. The time intervals are particularly hard to compare because the final seconds appear on a separate line.
critique.cause: The 205px metric column leaves too little text width for the checkout completion label. Each 110px interval column provides 89px of text width, less than the longest currency and time intervals need.

critique.good: The wider, equally sized interval columns give the paired estimates more room and preserve the symmetry of the comparison groups. Headers and individual numeric values remain intact.
critique.problems: The extra interval space does not keep the currency or time intervals on one line, but the narrower metric column makes cart abandonment wrap as well. More rows become tall without a corresponding improvement in interval readability.
critique.cause: At 120px, each interval column still has only 99px of text width, below the longest one-line interval widths. Reducing the metric column to 185px leaves insufficient room for the cart abandonment label.

critique.good: The 215px metric column keeps checkout completion and cart abandonment on one line, making the row labels easier to scan. The two comparison groups remain balanced, and the compact percentage intervals and summary values stay intact.
critique.problems: The currency and time intervals wrap in both groups, separating parts of the values readers need to compare. The time endpoints split across lines, which is especially disruptive.
critique.cause: The 105px interval columns provide only 84px of text width; the longest intervals need up to 113px. The extra width given to the metric column comes directly from those interval columns.

critique.good: The metric column gives labels a strong anchor: checkout completion and cart abandonment remain on one line. The paired groups are balanced, and means, lift values and p-values remain intact.
critique.problems: Both currency intervals wrap, and both time intervals split the second endpoint across lines, making those values harder to compare. Several long metric labels still wrap.
critique.cause: The 108px and 107px confidence-interval columns provide only 87px and 86px of text space; the 210px metric column takes space that could widen them.

critique.good: Both currency and time intervals stay on one line, so control and variant estimates are easy to compare. Corresponding columns have similar proportions, and numeric values remain intact.
critique.problems: Most metric labels wrap, including three that fit on one line in r2A. The narrow label column makes the table feel tall and gives the row identifiers less visual weight.
critique.cause: The 160px metric column provides 139px of text space, while the 134px and 131px interval columns receive enough room for the longest intervals.

critique.good: The paired estimate groups remain balanced, numeric summaries stay intact, and cart abandonment fits on one line.
critique.problems: Checkout completion wraps in addition to the longer labels, while the currency and time intervals still wrap much as they do in r2A. The wider interval columns therefore do not resolve the most conspicuous numeric breaks.
critique.cause: Reducing the metric column to 200px crosses the checkout-label wrapping threshold, but 115px and 110px are still too narrow for the longest intervals.

r0A.idea: Preserve every numeric value and confidence interval on one line, using a narrow metric column that wraps longer labels.

r0B.idea: Give metric labels more room while treating the two confidence interval columns equally and allowing their longest ranges to wrap.

r0C.idea: Prioritize readable metric labels and compact paired comparison columns, accepting more wrapping in confidence intervals.

r1A.idea: Refine r0B by giving the time means and p-value header enough width, while returning some metric space to both intervals. This should preserve most of r0B's compact row rhythm and improve the readability of longer values.

r1B.idea: Give both interval columns more room while keeping the means and p-value header intact. Some metric labels will wrap, but this explores whether fewer interval breaks produce a clearer comparison.

r1C.idea: Keep the metric column close to r0B's width while fixing the split time means and p-value header. The longest intervals may still wrap, providing a direct comparison with the more interval-focused alternatives.

r2A.idea: Refine r1C by moving 5px from the metric column into the interval columns. Check whether checkout completion still fits while giving the paired intervals slightly more breathing room.

r2B.idea: Give each interval enough text width for its longest one-line value. This tests the alternative of keeping all intervals together at the cost of more metric-label wrapping.

r2C.idea: Shift a little space from the metric column and variant interval to the control interval. This tests whether a modestly wider control interval improves its wrapping while retaining a reasonably broad row-label column.

r3A.idea: Test whether a small transfer from the metric column to the control interval improves its wrapping while preserving the useful label fit seen in r2A.

r3B.idea: Give both interval columns more room than in r2A while retaining more space for labels than in r2B. This tests whether better interval breaks justify additional label wrapping.

r3C.idea: Test an asymmetric allocation that favors the slightly longer control intervals while keeping a wider metric column than r2B; inspect whether the resulting breaks and group proportions remain comfortable.

contrast.idea: The metric column has only 79px for text, less than the longest unbreakable word. Labels would split within words or overflow, while the confidence-interval columns would have excess space.

understanding.purpose: Compare checkout outcomes for the control and variant, including uncertainty, relative lift and statistical significance.
understanding.reading: Readers scan each metric across its row, comparing the two means and confidence intervals before checking lift and p-value. Longer metric labels can use multiple lines; the two-tier header already occupies extra height.
groups: Control Mean and 95% CI belong together as the estimate and its uncertainty; Variant Mean and 95% CI play the same roles and should have comparable widths.
Lift and p-value are compact summaries of the comparison for each metric.
Metric labels identify the row and anchor the comparisons across it.
keep_intact: Individual means, percentages, currency amounts, p-values and lift values.
Time values and numeric identifiers such as 1,000.
Confidence intervals where space permits, especially the time and currency intervals.
may_wrap: Confidence intervals at natural break points if needed, keeping each endpoint intact.
The p-value header if its column is too narrow.

bad.why: The metric column has only 79px for text, less than the longest unbreakable word. Labels would split within words or overflow, while the confidence-interval columns would have excess space.

contrast.why: The metric column has only 79px for text, less than the longest unbreakable word. Labels would split within words or overflow, while the confidence-interval columns would have excess space.

final.rationale: r2B keeps both confidence intervals on one line, making the control and variant results easier to compare across each row. Its narrower metric column wraps most labels, but the breaks remain readable and the labels still identify their rows clearly. The two result groups have closely matched proportions, and the headers remain intact.

general: Give columns enough width to keep values that readers compare as units together when the available space permits.
Columns with corresponding roles should have comparable proportions, while longer row labels can use natural word breaks.
Judge wrapping by its effect on scanning and meaning, rather than by table height alone.
specific: The control and variant confidence intervals need approximately 134px and 131px respectively to keep their longest entries on one line.
The metric labels can wrap at words without mid-word splits in the displayed candidates.

final.tradeoffs: r2B produces a taller table and wraps more metric labels than r1C or r2A. A designer who prioritizes scanning the metric names over keeping confidence intervals intact could reasonably prefer one of those alternatives.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates around r2B, not independently rendered tests. They describe small coupled adjustments that preserve the overall proportions and 719px limit; their endpoints are not intended to be combined freely.

A.why: The confidence intervals have ample room, but the narrow metric column breaks words and stretches labels across three or four lines, making rows difficult to scan.

B.why: Metric labels remain readable and the two test groups are balanced, but the currency and time confidence intervals split across lines, making comparisons harder.

C.why: Both groups have balanced proportions, all numeric values and intervals stay on one line, and metric labels wrap naturally without breaking words.

D.why: Nearly equal column widths waste space on short values while breaking a metric word and splitting several confidence intervals; the tall rows are hard to scan.

E.why: The wider metric column keeps most labels compact and the groups balanced, though currency and time confidence intervals wrap across lines.

F.why: Metric labels are compact, but the p-value header, time means, and several confidence intervals wrap, disrupting the comparison of results.

reviews.unsure: B and E make a reasonable tradeoff for wider metric labels, but the split confidence intervals make them less effective for comparing results.

A.why: The narrow metric column breaks “abandonment” inside the word and forces several labels into three or four lines. Some confidence intervals also wrap, making rows harder to scan.

B.why: Confidence intervals stay on one line, but the very narrow metric column splits words such as “completion” and “abandonment” and makes the table unnecessarily tall.

C.why: Metric labels remain intact and the paired groups are balanced, but the currency and time confidence intervals wrap, splitting time values across lines.

D.why: A generous metric column keeps most labels short, and corresponding control and variant columns align well. Currency and time intervals still wrap, with time values split across lines.

E.why: The metric labels have useful space, but both time means split over two lines, as do the time intervals, and the p-value header wraps.

F.why: All means and confidence intervals stay intact on one line, while metric labels wrap naturally without breaking words. The control and variant groups have balanced widths and rows remain easy to compare.

reviews.unsure: D gives the metric labels more room, so its wider first column could be preferred if label scanning matters more than keeping confidence intervals intact.
